important.name: Engine tests never exercise the git top-level probe or the root-candidate order in watch.ts
important.summary: `world()` always answers `process.run` with exit 128 and sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and `session.cwd` to the same ROOT. A regression in watch.ts, such as ignoring a successful git answer, swapping env and cwd in the call, or failing to trim the trailing newline, would leave a worktree session silently inactive while every test passes. The root.ts header promises that behavior.

important.name: apply overwrites hand-edited References on every rerun
important.summary:
The driver docstring says apply writes facts over TODO(fill) stubs, but apply_facts replaces References with stubbed_only=False, and cmd_apply replays every facts/*.json each run. After a scaffold rerun plus apply, earlier References corrections by the developer or memo reviewer are silently lost.

Also (overall): apply_facts replaces References unconditionally (stubbed_only=False, bubble_memo.py:605-606) and cmd_apply feeds it every facts/*.json in scratch (scripts/bubble_memo.py:483-497). On a skill rerun (new bubble, scaffold, investigator, apply), every older flagged entry has its References reverted to the investigator list, undoing step 4 or step 7 corrections, and check does not notice. Contradicts SKILL.md step 3 (touches only entries whose stubs remain), the snapshot rule, the driver docstring and plan BM-3. test_bubble_memo.py:229-235 pins the overwrite; no rerun test.

Also (system_shape): apply_facts (commit 42ef747) replaces the References field of an entry whenever a facts file exists (stubbed_only=False), and cmd_apply replays every facts/*.json on each run. The skill Step 3 (writes each report over the TODO(fill) stubs and touches only entries whose facts exist and whose stubs remain), the driver docstring (apply writes each report into its memo entry over the TODO(fill) stubs) and plan BM-3 (apply_facts replaces only the flagged entry stubs) all promise the opposite. Skill Step 4 tells the session to correct References that moved and Step 7 applies reviewer accuracy corrections by hand; any later apply (for example after a redispatched investigator) silently reverts those corrections to the investigator text, the spec anti-goal of overwriting the drafting agent prose.

Also (roast): apply_facts calls _replace_field(block, _REFERENCES, ..., stubbed_only=False), so every `apply` run overwrites the References line of each entry that has a facts report, even when no stub is left. The rest of the PR says otherwise: SKILL.md step 3 says apply 'touches only entries whose facts exist and whose stubs remain', the driver docstring (scripts/bubble_memo.py:20-21) says it writes 'over the TODO(fill) stubs', plan BM-3 says it 'replaces only the flagged entry's ... stubs', and spec Section 1 repeats that. The result is that References corrected by hand in step 4 or after a reviewer accuracy finding in step 7 go back to the investigator's version when apply runs again, and cmd_apply reports that id as 'applied'. On a CRLF memo, apply_facts also returns LF text even when nothing changed, so every rerun rewrites the file. No test covers a second apply after a hand edit. The memo's whole job is to be correct, and this quietly undoes corrections.

Also (runtime): The docstring says LF endings only when text changed, yet apply_facts returns the LF join whenever the entry exists. On a CRLF memo cmd_apply lists the first id as applied and rewrites the file with no field filled.

Also (system_shape): The module docstring says text returned by apply_facts uses LF endings only when it changed, but apply_facts always returns the LF-joined lines once the entry exists. cmd_apply compares updated != text, so on a CRLF memo the first facts report is listed under applied and the memo is rewritten on every run even when the facts were already applied.
fix: Replace References only while it still holds the scaffold pre-fill (_reference_line output) or a TODO(fill) stub.
Or skip facts whose entry has no stub left, and fix the driver docstring to say References are replaced.

In apply_facts, leave an entry with no TODO(fill) untouched, and replace References only when it still equals the scaffold prefill or holds a stub; add a driver test that hand-edits References between two apply runs and asserts the edit survives.
Have cmd_apply skip entries with no stub left and report only ids whose stubs it filled.

Gate the References replacement: replace only when the field still holds a STUB or still equals the scaffold-rendered _reference_line(issue) text, so a hand-corrected References survives a rerun of apply.

Or keep the behavior and update SKILL.md Step 3, the scripts/bubble_memo.py module docstring and plan BM-3 (through plan.py, then re-render the PIP) to say References are always replaced from the facts, and tell the skill never to rerun apply after hand edits.

In apply_facts, return the text unchanged when the entry block holds no STUB (an early `return text` when STUB is absent from the joined block lines). The first apply still replaces the pre-filled References, as commit 42ef747 intends, and later runs leave hand edits alone. Add a lib test: apply, hand-edit References, apply again, and assert the text is unchanged.

Or keep the behavior and make the documents match it: SKILL.md step 3, the driver docstring for `apply`, and plan BM-3 (through plan.py) say that References are always replaced and that apply must not run after hand corrections.
Return the original text when the rebuilt block equals the original span lines.
In apply_facts, build the output and return the original text when the output equals _lf(text).

important.name: entry_flagged claims to apply check's rule but scans the whole entry, not References
important.summary:
The entry_flagged docstring says it applies 'the rule `check` applies: the JSON rule, or References naming several files'. In fact it runs memo_references(block) over the whole entry: Current behavior, Chain, Expected behavior and Recommendation. check_memo (_entry_problems) counts files only in the References field. Take a non-flagged entry whose Current behavior cites a second file in backticks. check passes it without a Chain, but reviewer_row marks it flagged and dispatches opus, and the reviewer brief prints '(flagged: yes)' for an entry with no Chain. The reviewer will likely file an accuracy finding for the missing chain, which forces the second round that decision D9 tries to avoid. These are two copies of one rule that disagree, and the docstring says they agree.

Also (runtime): entry_flagged claims the rule check applies, but memo_references uses the driver _TOKEN_RE, which does not strip spaces in a code span, while check_memo strips spans before REF_RE.fullmatch. A space-padded path:line span changes the file count only in check, so the reviewer model can disagree with check.

Also (overall): Docstring: the rule check applies (References naming several files). Code: memo_references over the whole block (scripts/bubble_memo.py:200-203, 376-383), while check reads only the References field (bubble_memo.py:421-426). A second-file path:line in Current behavior or Chain makes reviewer_row print opus and the brief say flagged: yes for an entry check treats as unflagged.

Also (system_shape): The entry_flagged docstring says it applies the check rule (the JSON rule, or References naming several files), but memo_references(block) collects every backticked path:line span anywhere in the entry (Current behavior, Chain, expected-behavior lines). check_memo counts only the References field (_field_text(lines, _REFERENCES)). An entry whose Chain cites a second file is reported as flagged: yes in the reviewer brief and pushes the reviewer model to opus, while check never demanded a chain for it.
fix: Add a public helper to harness_lib.bubble_memo, `reference_files(block: str) -> List[str]`, defined as _reference_files(_reference_tokens(_field_text(lines, _REFERENCES) or '')). Use it in both _entry_problems and the driver's entry_flagged so the flag rule exists in one place. Keep memo_references over the whole block only for the reviewer's excerpts.
Build memo_references from bm._TOKEN_RE spans, stripped, that fullmatch bm.REF_RE; drop the driver _TOKEN_RE.
Add one public helper in harness_lib.bubble_memo that returns the distinct files of the References field and use it in both _entry_problems and entry_flagged.

Move the entry-level flag into harness_lib.bubble_memo (one function reading _reference_files(_reference_tokens(_field_text(lines, _REFERENCES)))) and call it from both _entry_problems and the driver entry_flagged / reviewer_row / _entry_table.

important.name: Skill says apply only fills stubs, but apply_facts always rewrites References
important.summary: SKILL.md step 3 says apply writes each report 'over the TODO(fill) stubs' and 'touches only entries whose facts exist and whose stubs remain'. At the head, apply_facts calls _replace_field(..., _REFERENCES, ..., stubbed_only=False) (bubble_memo.py:605-606), and its docstring says References are replaced even when the scaffold pre-filled them. cmd_apply also loops over every facts/*.json in the PR's scratch folder. So any rerun of apply (a redispatched investigator, or a second skill run after scaffold appends new bubbles) puts the investigator's old References back into every earlier flagged entry. That undoes corrections the session made in step 4 or step 7 from reviewer findings, and apply counts those ids as applied. The skill's snapshot rule ('never regenerated over existing text') and the driver docstring ('over the TODO(fill) stubs') both say this cannot happen.
fix: Limit the References overwrite in apply_facts to entries that still hold a TODO(fill) stub, for example by checking STUB in the entry block before replacing, so a finished entry is left alone. Then the skill text is accurate as written.

Or keep the overwrite and correct the docs: SKILL.md step 3 says References are always replaced from the recorded facts, even outside stubs, and warns that rerunning apply undoes hand corrections to References of entries that have facts. Change the bubble_memo.py module docstring for apply to match.

minor.name: Edit/Write trigger misses undiscovered memos
minor.summary:
discover() runs only from afterShell (REVIEW_SCRIPT: pr_review.py, review_edit.py) and session.start; bubble_memo.py scaffold does not match. A memo scaffolded mid-session whose review JSON is then changed by Edit/Write is not in the active set, so afterFile returns and turn.complete checks an empty set; the stamp waits for the next session or review-script call.

Also (overall): Spec Section 4 and plan BM-8: list the folder whenever a trigger shows an unknown memo. Only session.start and shell calls naming pr_review.py or review_edit.py run discover (stamp.ts:29, 182-196); bubble_memo.py scaffold is not matched, and Edit/Write and turn.complete only check known memos (stamp.ts:199-204, 232-236). A decision recorded by editing the review JSON in the same session waits for the next session start. README.md:77-78 documents it.

Also (system_shape): Spec Section 4 says the folder is listed whenever a trigger shows a memo not yet known, but only shell calls naming pr_review.py or review_edit.py run discover; bubble_memo.py scaffold (the only writer of memos) does not match REVIEW_SCRIPT, and Edit/Write of a review JSON and turn.complete only run checkAll over the already-known set. A decision recorded by editing the review JSON right after scaffolding stays unstamped until the next session start or pr_review.py call. The README lists this as a known limitation rather than closing it.

Also (roast): REVIEW_SCRIPT matches only pr_review.py and review_edit.py, and turn.complete only checks memos already known; it never lists the folder. A memo created mid-session by `bubble_memo.py scaffold`, which is the only command that creates memos, stays unknown until the next session start or the next pr_review.py or review_edit.py call. Until then, an Edit or Write of its review JSON stamps nothing, because afterFile matches only active memos. Spec Section 4 says the folder is listed 'whenever a trigger shows a memo not yet known'. The README lists this gap under known limitations when the fix is a single regex alternative.
fix: Add bubble_memo.py as a REVIEW_SCRIPT alternative.
Or have afterFile run scan through serial() when the path is a NNNN_*.json in the reviews folder that no active memo names.
Add bubble_memo.py to the REVIEW_SCRIPT regex, add a stamp.test.ts case, and narrow the README limitation.

minor.summary:

Or accept the unpadded prefix and the name tie-break in reviewFileFor.

Rename the reviewer test to match its three words, or assert only the two lens names the driver brief uses.

minor.name: Agent contract test never names the agent files, so PR CI skips it on agent edits
minor.summary: The test builds each path as `f{name}.md` from `_AGENTS = (bubble-memo-investigator, bubble-memo-reviewer)`. `tools/select_tests.py` `mentions()` matches a changed file by its full basename (the bare-stem fallback applies only to .py files), and this test does not walk the tree. Neither `bubble-memo-investigator.md` nor `bubble-memo-reviewer.md` appears in the source. A PR that edits only `plugins/harness/agents/bubble-memo-*.md` therefore never selects this test, and a broken frontmatter or a dropped read-only rule shows up only after the merge to main. CLAUDE.md requires a test that reaches a file through a runtime-built path to spell the file name out.
